bio: Aeris and the Piggies are a 5-piece indie/folk group based out of Minneapolis. They focus on warm, acoustic, and experimental sounds, as well as narrative-driven songwriting in their music.

Angel Shot is a metalcore band from Minneapolis that brings raw intensity, heavy grooves, and clever songwriting to the table. By mixing modern metalcore and noise.
they’ve been gaining traction in the Twin Cities scene with powerful releases like “Gate of Mercy” and “Stray” featuring Soulkeeper. They’re known for their high-energy live shows and a DIY approach, delivering a visceral, in your face performance that resonates with both hardcore fans and newcomers.

Annie and the Bang Bang are a Minneapolis rock band. Inspired by songs on car radios during family road trips in the ‘70s, and mixtapes they made in the '90s, they’re a little Fleetwood Mac meets Nirvana or Heart meets R.E.M. A lyrically cinematic, riff-heavy, sonic adventure. Sometimes you gotta feel good.

Conceived in 2021, launched in 2025, Anxiety Society has blasted out of the starting gate with four anthemic singles which have been described as "millenial Nine Inch Nails" and "...an infectious dark-toned sound that could have been birthed from code of the The Matrix."

Rest assured though, the band is 100% human. Operating from the northern American midwest tundra of Minneapolis, Adam Szczepaniak, Jeremy Montoya, Matt Greeninger, and Jonathan Kennedy utilize their tools to craft a loud, raw, yet musically tight sonic landscape, both in the studio and on the stage.

Their debut EP, “Pull,” dropped in December 2025, instantly turning heads.

Jon Peterson started Arcola in 2005. The band has taken a few different forms over the past 20 years. Arcola just wrapped up its third album and they are excited to branch out from an indie-Americana sound to more rollicking rock & roll textures.

genre: Jazz, Funk, Blues, RnB...and even a little Butt Rock
bio:
Who is Art Beagle? What does he do?
Why does he have a back up band? Never mind about him.

Art is just a guy who sits in a chair, drinks beer and watches TV.

Art Beagle's Backup Band is....

Keys/Lead Vocals - Michael Burton
Bass/Sax/Backup Vocals - Tamir Nolley
Drums - Yoji Sera

Art Beagle's Backup Band plays a variety of styles and will soon have an EP out this summer.

Astronomy Town’s fusion of indie, jazz, showgaze, and midwest emo pairs hypnotic rhythms with lush harmonies to recreate the soundscape of a city where residents bustle at night and the stars are always visible... known as Astronomy Town.

Astronomy Town is Cassandra Johnson, Robb Lauer, Michael Mooridian, and Joe Twohy.
Atomic Lights began in the summer of 2012.  High speed rock and roll with a knack for the noisier side of things.  Stay loud.

B n’ the Spice Cabinet is a funk-pop original band that includes a lively horn section and intricately smooth vocal lines and harmonies. Based out of Minneapolis, the band pulls influence from artists such as Stevie Wonder, Sara Bareilles, and Lawrence, to name a few. Led by Milwaukee native Bridget Cushman, the band continues to explore the Minneapolis Metro performing throughout the cities, bringing the funk to venues such as Minnesota Music Cafe, the Amsterdam, and Utepils Brewing. Get ready to dance and have some fun with this energetic group of college friends turned bandmates!
Sad, but catchy.

Welcome:
BirdLand is a community-based, anti-capitalist artistic venture driven by Casey "Bird" Schultz and Robin Hatterschide. The idea behind BirdLand was simple: build a  sanctuary where people can feel free to express themselves and genuinely connect with one another. We place our emphasis squarely on community, rather than fandom, using our music as the connective tissue that brings us all together.

The Sound:
Musically, our cross-genre compositions are focused heavily on raw energy and expression. Rooted in the improvisational freedom of our jazz upbringing, we draw heavily on the driving grooves of EDM, the defiance and drive of rock, and the undeniable stank of funk. We use these influences, along with our synths, keys, and drums, as a paintbrush; creating auditory imagery and leaving the listener to discover their own meaning in the sound.

ETHOS: 
BirdLand operates on the foundational principles of P.L.U.R. (Peace, Love, Unity, Respect). We are inclusive as far as our kindness reaches, protecting our sanctuary by ensuring hatred never finds a foothold.

Our commitment to our community also means a hard rejection of the modern digital landscape. We do not believe in social media, and we refuse to be packaged as currency or as a product for tech oligarchs. The techno-fascists have found something that sells better than sex, and that’s rage. We refuse to contribute a single drop of energy to a space that thrives on anger, as it goes against our foundation

The Escape:
While Robin and Casey are slaves to the capitalist machine, we have found an escape from our corporate Over-lords within birdland. We would love to share this escape with you. If your curious, come out, get loud, and see what we are all about.

band_name: Bobby J's West Bank Social Club
bio: Dance music from a bygone era.  A six-piece, typical New Orleans style bar band with horns, playing jazzy dance music, lounge ballads, and a little bit of mambo. Bobby J’s West Bank Social Club was born at Palmer's Bar on the West Bank in Minneapolis.

Carhearts is an all-girl indie rock band based in Minneapolis. Drawing inspiration from bands like The Backseat Lovers, Big Thief, and Foo Fighters, Carhearts blends raw energy with intimate songwriting. Whether it's busking around the Twin Cities or playing at your local house party, Carhearts always puts on a show.

A consummate storyteller and captivating live performer, singer-songwriter and composer Carlisle Evans Peck is a musician grounded in queer mythic storytelling somewhere at the meeting of music theater and bardic balladry. Gender and genre-bending, their queer glam-folk-rock musical style is a singular melding of the ethereal folk echoes of the likes of Joanna Newsom and Sufjan Stevens with a glamorous theatrical drama and maximalism reminiscent of Freddy Mercury and David Bowie. Carlisle has released four records including the 2025 release The Lines in My Hands, toured their work regionally and nationally including the 2024 ritual cabaret Iconoclasm, and composed for choirs, bands, and theater ensembles around the region. For their musical intuition, innovation, and inspiration, collaborators have granted them the nickname “The Magician”.

Originally a Power Trio for the last four years including 2025s 
Uptown Porchfest Performance we added a veteran Lead Singer to
Christmas on Neptune and we couldn't be more ecstatic with the results!
Cant wait to hit the streets of Minneapolis for 2026 Uptown Porchfest! 💕✌️

Common Lady, formed from Midwest friends-of-friends, makes their debut with their first EP, Patchwork. The songs began as singer-songwriter Emma Deihl’s quiet reflections—soft reckonings with the constant becoming of one’s twenties, where change, heartbreak, and celebration blur together. At first simple, acoustic chords and vocal melodies, the songs longed for a sound expansive enough to hold the full emotional swell behind them. Thus, Emma sought musicians to bring her musings to life, and Common Lady was born. Blending elements of jazz, folk, and pop, Common Lady collectively crafts simultaneously catchy and deeply felt songs, reaching for relatability without sacrificing lyrical specificity. Produced by Sam Tudor, who also plays drums and adds violin to the record, the music is shaped by Andrew Bien’s luminous jazz piano and Michael Vandervennet’s steady, soulful bass. Together, Common Lady creates music that feels both intimate and shared: tender stories unfolding within a rich, collaborative landscape of sound.
Short, catchy songs about Movies, TV Shows, and Video Games. Couch Potato Massacre tries to have fun singing about having fun and show love while singing about love.
Generating heat since 2022, Critterthing has a positive message coded in melodic sunspots violently etched onto the mind.

Customers are a Minneapolis rock band formed in the mid ‘90s. Signed to Neil Young’s Vapor Records, the band toured with Ben Folds Five, Iggy Pop, and played festivals in Europe featuring Young and Pearl Jam. Customers also appeared on The Conan O’Brien Show. The band's EP “Living Like Gods,” produced by Dan Murphy, comes out in 5/22/26.

DKTK stands for Dont kill your inner child. We are a 2 member band, our first album is with Doug on lead vocals and guitar, with Kyra on drums doing backing vocals. Our 2nd album titled "You Look Fine" is Kyra playing Guitar and doing Lead vocals, with Doug on drums..

Damn Phibian is not a band defined by boundaries. The five piece indie rock band draws influences from a wide range of musical ethos, including 70s Krautrock, 80s City Pop, and all of that good 90s Britpop. Add a large dose of funk and you get groovy beats, textured guitars, and funky time signatures that'll get you dancing introspectively.
Mellow band based on three part vocal harmonies and catchy original songwriting.

Dread Spells is a four piece post-rock band from Minneapolis, MN. Featuring members of local bands Vanishing Earth and Jupiter Johnson, Dread Spells was formed in 2024 and is a project focused on combining the influences of its members into an emotionally evocative live musical experience combined with visual media.

Drift Pattern—a band that blends post-punk and post-hardcore with a whole lot of influences. Our members come from backgrounds like doom metal, indie rock, and singer-songwriter, so you get a mix of heavy riffs, catchy melodies, and honest lyrics.

Eldest Daughter is a Twin-Cities based indie rock band fronted by Monica Merila.
After forming in 2024, we released our debut EP, Cactus Magnet, in January 2025. We are currently in the process of promoting our first studio EP, The Year of the Swan.

Emily Boyajian is a composer who uses her strong background in music theory to write music that is intellectually stimulating and emotionally captivating. She has written solo piano works, chamber music, orchestral music, and art songs. She has had her music performed at the 2019 Source Song Festival, the 2021 and 2023 Film Score Fest, the 2023 Cedar Commissions, the 2024 Minnesota Fringe Festival, and in other concerts in the Twin Cities. Her songs focus on topics such as her experiences as a trans woman, contemporary political and social issues, and silly songs about things such as Delta Airlines and arguing with a sock puppet.

FLOWTUS, revived in 2022, is a queer four-piece dreamy indie rock ensemble featuring Janani Logendran on lead vocals and electric guitar, Erin Horvath on lead electric guitar and vocals, Katya Haskina on bass and vocals, and Kelsey Wefald on drums. Their sound blends melancholic, sultry vibes with an energetic, raw edge, capturing the complexities of love and heartbreak.

Fairborn Sinfonia is named after an Ohio city and was started in CA, but is in a way based in Minneapolis now. They have been making music since at least 2010 which if you do the math is a very long time. The music is experimental and ambient and also drone and also lo-fi and also noise and also slowcore which is a lot of genres for one band to be doing but they are doing all of them. Field recordings from across the globe have been layered in live. The globe has been viewed in many cities.

Albums have been recorded in living rooms in Palo Alto and Minneapolis and also Fairborn. Multiple different living rooms. The objects in the living rooms were used as instruments and have not been credited which is something that may need to be addressed at some point. A monotron was also used. If you do not know what a monotron is thats okay you can look it up.

The project has released music under several names. There are reasons for this. All releases are name your price which in most cases has meant no price and that is fine. New content is upcoming and incredible. Thank you for your interest in this website.

Pushing the envelope with his catchy rap steeze "AfroTrap", Fanaka Nation is a rising star in the Minneapolis music scene. A product of immigrant parents hailing from Kenya and Laos, he attributes his sounds to growing up in Minnesota and constantly having world music playing in his home (ranging from Soukouss style to Mor Lum rhythms). 

His newly released single "Blicky Love" is an infectious, shoulder swaying, and unwrinkled Afro pop tune about playing Russian roulette with a love that is wishy washy. This joint features the brilliant local artist Bakarii. 

Fanaka is also the co-founder & host of "MPLS afrobeats". A dance party entered around local afro music & culture. Each night also features a local performer. 

Back by his band, "The Wawa's", these musicians are the "live machine" behind Fanaka's compositions. The most senior members of the band consist of Robert Lehmann (keyboard), and Derrick Holleman (electric guitar). The band are currently working on their first project as a group!

Introducing, Fever Field: a pop sensation from Minneapolis, Minnesota. Founded by lead vocalist, Jack Cassidy, and  drummer, Drew Lodermeier, in November of 2022, Fever Field delivers a groove and feel-good wall of sound that will leave listeners with a smile on their face.

Minneapolis-based singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Frankie Torres has been performing for over 17 years. Her modern take on blues and rock have been seen on notable stages such as Red Rocks Amphitheatre, Lollaoalooza, The Taste of Minnesota, and NBC’s The Voice. Frankie was a contestant on season 26 of the show, where she earned a coveted “4 chair turn” with her powerful rendition of Heart’s “Magic Man”. Frankie’s unique songwriting skills, high-energy stage presence, and impressive vocal talent make her an up and coming musician to keep an eye on!

Delicate and defying, Gill Weather (formerly Oceanographer) is a love letter to 90’s dream pop, small town origins, and bittersweet memories. 
their lush folk soundscape is steeped in sharp and poignant storytelling, welcoming listeners into a “midwest gothic” dreamworld— one where the pink sunset is eclipsed by power lines and fast-food signs, teenagers honeymoon in the football field across the creek, and unrequited love becomes a dead-end job and a baby on the way.

Gill Weather was a 2025 Nominee at The Loring Awards for “Best Upcoming Artist,” as well as a recipient of a 2026 Cedar Cultural Center Flagship Grant. 

Gill Weather is made up by: Valentine Lowry-Ortega, Willow Waters, Dean Sibinski, Jackson Peters, and Joe Kiser.

HUNNY BEAR is a jazz fusion quartet located in Minneapolis, MN. Featuring a combination of styles and performing music ranging from modern covers, funk standards, fresh sounds and originals, everyone is sure to enjoy the cool vibes and energy at any performance.
 
Featuring Dan Anderson on saxophone and vocals, Dan Abel on guitar,  J Cole Blodgett on bass guitar and Ryan Vee on drums, this group has been a part of Open Streets and the Music in the Parks series, and can be seen at a number of venues in the metro area including, but not limited to, 331 Club, The White Squirrel Bar, Can Can Wonderland  and many more.

Homers Donuts is an all girl tween and young teen band from Minneapolis that came together through Twin Town Guitars' Bridge Powered Girl Band program. Playing songs by Metric, Nirvana, and other rock favorites, they're fueled by friendship, loud guitars, and the excitement of performing live.

Honey Please is an indie pop rock band out of Minneapolis, Minnesota. Through a shared joy of musical expression and a love of performing, they have delighted many ears around the Twin Cities area. All original songs are written by singer-guitarist Sam Scheuneman who has been writing songs since he learned to speak. Bassist Dawson Ludvigson adds intricate bass melodies under a light melody sung by Sam. Guitarist Jack Nobel shreds lead lines to give each song its unique timbre. On the drums, Joe Kiser continues to keep beats fresh and alive with a lively and energetic tone. Together these musicians create a sound that feels complete and is full of emotion. When playing live the audience just cannot stop dancing and moving along to the beat. Honey Please released their first studio album in October '24 and is planning a follow up EP for Spring '26.

IdlFlo is a four-piece alt-rock wrecking crew from Minneapolis. Formed in 2019 and built on raw grit and contrast, they shift from whisper-quiet to explosive in a heartbeat. Their style is fueled by roaring riffs, huge hooks, and layered harmonies that echo the restless energy and angst of ’90s alternative. Known for hard-hitting performances that leave a mark, you can expect energy, no backing tracks and no safety nets -  just raw original alternative rock!

Iodine is a four-piece alternative rock band from the twin cities. Their music is diverse, with inspirations spanning pop rock like Hippo Campus, to the technicality and improvisation of King Gizzard, and the energy of midwest emo/math rock groups like American Football or Delta Sleep. The focus of the band is on each of its individual members each bringing very distinct tastes and rich personalities (both musical and otherwise) to the stage for a performance that is accessible for all kinds of fans, whether it be moshers, theory nerds, or people who just want to have a few drinks and a good time. 

Iodine has been active since early 2025, debuting their first grunge  single Vice Grip/Washed Away later that year. They have since released another single and live album recorded at the Twin Cities own Green Room and are slowly making their way into the Twin Cities music scene.

band_name: J-Mo On The Beat & The J-Lighters
bio:
Hailing from Saint Paul, Minnesota, Jamie’s music effortlessly blends the classic 50s and 60s vibes with contemporary rock and pop elements, creating a unique and captivating sound. Influenced by legendary artists such as Elvis Presley, Little Richard, Michael Jackson, Cliff Richard, and Billy Fury, Jamie’s musical journey began at a tender age with dancing, eventually blossoming into a fervent desire to become a music artist during his high school years.
With the unwavering support of his talented backing band, The J-Lighters, who skillfully capture the essence of the 50s sound, Jamie confidently ventures into the music scene.
The jay boys family band play the toe tapping tunes you didn't know you love.

Jessica Forsythe is a Minneapolis-based songwriter and musician best known for her years as a touring drummer with Sick of Sarah, performing throughout the U.S., Canada, and the UK, including appearances at Warped Tour and SXSW.

After stepping away from music for several years, she has returned with a new focus on songwriting and guitar. Joined by acoustic musician Jon Stack, the duo blends original indie/alternative songs with tight vocal harmonies and two-guitar arrangements, creating an intimate yet engaging live performance.

Years ago, John Magnuson was in a Minneapolis band called the Carpetbaggers. John wrote and sang many of the band's songs. In November of 2020, John released an Americana Indie/Folk-Rock-ish record (with splashes of twang) called "Barely Noticeable". In 2024, he released "Waiting For The Water To Recede", another fine Americana/Folk-Rock release. His eponymous trio+ consists of Paul McFarland (Run Westy Run, Lolo's Ghost), John Sandbo (Curtiss A and the Dark Click), JJ Benson (Lolo's Ghost, Scott Allen and the List), and Jane Meyer on harmony vocals.

This is KVNT, the K is pronounced like a C and the V like a U- now you figure the rest out. KVNT is composed of the ethereal vocalist Mariana, guitarist Brandon (of Samuel John Band), bassist Mackenzie, and drummer Cartier (of Todd and many more). A storm of their collective creative energy is on full display on stage as they work to empower the metal scene against the patriarchy. Their sound combines metal and industrial music with a fem-punk attitude.

Hey there, my name is Kai Lok (“kay-lock”) and I'm a Minneapolis music artist embedding my truth and value into song. I’m passionate about being emotionally vulnerable as a man, as a person struggling with depression, and an advocate for authenticity. Since I was a teenager, music has been a therapeutic tool for me, as I navigate overwhelming voices in my head and seek ways to release and keep going. My favorite places to be are on stages and in community. I love to connect with people and bring a room to life through call-and-response songs, live lyric videos, energetic raps, and unapologetic vulnerability. With power comes responsibility, so I try hard to be intentional about how I use my platform (online or in-person). I want people to know they are not alone and that they are human beings worthy of love and respect. I want to create spaces for other people to shine and grow. I want to build bridges of commonality, and find the humanity in each and every one of us.
6 people playing a dozen or so instruments. Songs range from heartbreaking to terrifying to hilarious. For fans of Gogol Bordello, Harley Poe, and Tom Waits.

kvsket blends an expansive range of rock and metal stylings, transitioning from crushingly heavy to seductively intimate, often within the same song. Formed by four friends who, all looking for something more outside of their former bands and projects, came together to weave their sprawling influences and inspirations into a unique, raw and personal sound.

Land is an indie-folk collaboration between David Carnes (guitar, sounds, percussion, vocals) and Lisa Hirst Carnes (harmonium, keys, vocals). We create atmospheric, harmony-rich music with guitar, harmonium, keys, ambient textures, and beats.

I've been writing and playing music for a long time but this current project is more personal. All the songs I write and record in my basement and I'm just doing it for the love of the game. All my favorite songs have a bit of sadness to them and I'm trying to pull in the melancholy.

Lost Evidence is a Minneapolis-based hard rock band known for their chaos, chemistry and crunchy riffs. The 6-piece band mixes alternative rock, with punk, grunge, and metal, with occasional melodic and bluesy turns aided by two backup singers. Driven by heavy guitar riffs, punchy rhythms, and  provocative, sometimes sardonic lyrics, the band never takes itself seriously and always retains its sense of fun. 

They have recently released their third studio album, Exhibit A, across all major streaming platforms and on CD. The album explores themes of rebellion and loss and features a catchy punk singalong on the lead single "Sore Loser".

“This is a collaborative album where every song sounds different, and we lean into that. We collaborate with variety of lead singers and cross genres to create a dynamic, surprising musical journey,” says lead guitarist Mark McGinty.

Lost Evidence is based in Minneapolis, MN and has earned a reputation for their lively, high-energy raw performances in packed local clubs, supporting national acts like Psychostick and Green Jelly. They will support the new album in 2026 with a list of live performances in Minnesota and Wisconsin.

After a decade of playing gigs both large and small around the city of Chicago with indie rockers, Buckman Page, as well as with front porch folkers, Distant Brothers, Matty and his partner packed up their lives and moved to northeast Minneapolis in 2021. His current musical project, "Matty & The Subtle Validation" stems from something of a quest to find ways to connect with and to validate others through music. He's not an expert and it may not even be something he's very good at, but the bottom line is this: no matter who you are or where you're from, everyone deserves value.

Millennial Falcon is a fun alt-rock quintet based in the Twin Cities. Blending nostalgic grit with soulful melodies, they deliver a mix of powerful originals and reimagined covers. Their self-titled debut EP, released in August 2025, captures the raw, anthemic sound that has become their signature sound.

Javier Ramales is a Mexico-born,-based producer, DJ, independent label owner, creator of We Love Fiesta, and member of Opossum Colectivo, a collective that invites local artists to collaborate and create community-centered events. Rooted in the sounds, rhythms, and spirit of Latin America, his work blends bass-driven electronic music with influences from Mexico and across the region.

Driven by a deep love for fiesta, rhythm, and cultural connection, Javier creates music and spaces that celebrate Latino identity, community, and the energy of the dance floor. Deeply connected to the Minneapolis music scene while staying in tune with electronic movements across Latin America, his sound brings together movement, culture, and collaboration in a way that feels both local and global.

A garage punk band formed in Anoka, MN. Beloved acoustic artists “Lisa Bisbee” and “The Old Thompson Orchestra” join forces with Lorenzo Orduno(All Four Inches & Blveprints) to create the punk rock powerhouse known as POPSICLESTICK!
Sara Liebl  (a mess., Mild Manner) and Ian Menchaca (Animal D)  join forces to play old favorites and old not-favorites.

A community band with an impressive performance edge, the Pan‑handlers Steel Drum Band has been captivating audiences since their inception in 2014 with their vibrant Caribbean sound and diverse repertoire, including traditional steel pan tunes, The Beatles, Guns N’ Roses, and Prince. Experience the sweet, lively sound of the steel drums, which evolved from old oil barrels to the beautiful instruments we love today. Come and feel the rhythm only these instruments can create!

Prairie Potluck brings together decades of musical experience ranging from bluegrass, country, classical, Americana, gospel  and folk. The wide variety of musical genres was the inspiration for the name “Prairie Potluck”. Vocal harmonies and instrument abilities are the hallmark of this “Potluck of musicians”.  A Prairie Potluck performance brings out the joy of old time music, listening to story telling through their songs and warm feelings that can be felt as these musicians share their love of music from traditional bluegrass to contemporary country.

Members of Prairie Potluck include: Mark Fisher on banjo and guitar, Ruth Lawrence on guitar, Suki Sun on fiddle, John Kraft on bass, Vicki Andersen on Ukulele and Paul Meehl on mandolin. Mark is also a song writer and writes many of the bands songs.

Pretty Pretty Please is a Minneapolis indie rock band writing hook-driven songs with edge, attitude, and heart. Pulling from garage rock, indie, and alt-country influences, they bring a original and melodic sound that feels equally at home on a dive bar stage, a porch, or in your headphones.

Pyrmafrost is Minneapolis' sickest loremetal band! We combine sick Iron Maiden type riffs with epic grungey/alt metal basslines and also drums, which are fierce and galloping, and it's all just sick as frost. If you like songs about messed up creatures and high towers full of swords and stuff, then you might want to pop out for Porchfest, as we will bring the house down.

SECRET RIVERS features the vocals of Kyle “Guante” Tran Myhre backed by the live production wizardry of SEE MORE PERSPECTIVE on the MPC and Loop Station 505. As seen most recently on the No Kings 3 mainstage, the Twin Cities-based duo performs work that centers grounded, human connection—from rejecting dominant culture visions of masculinity, to affirming the importance of grief, to cultivating radical hope in the midst of crisis. Deftly weaving together Hip Hop, ambient, and a mural-like collage of vocal samples (from Octavia Butler, Avatar the Last Airbender, Blade Runner, and beyond), SMP arranges soundscapes for Tran Myhre’s words that feel right at home at a music festival, a theater show, a sci-fi convention, or the end/beginning of the world.

Selvedge is the finished edge of something raw. Where folk, Americana, rock, country, and blues meet without pretense. Guitar, bass, and voices. No filler. Every thread intentional.

Born out of front-porch sessions and dive bar sets in Minneapolis, we play the kind of music that sounds better on a warm night with the windows down. Genres are suggestions. Feeling is the point.

Seraphim is an up-and-coming heavy alt-rock band from St. Paul, Minnesota. Founded in January of 2026, this all-teenage group brings energy –and the musicianship– at every show they play. Fueled by drive and determination to make a splash on the local music scene, Seraphim blends undeniable technical skill and rocking energy to create a sound that’s impossible to ignore. With awesome guitar and basslines, epic drumming, and hard-hitting vocals, Seraphim is more than just a band. They’re musical excellence. And they’re just getting started.

Side.Door is a 5-piece fusion jazz band that brings a fresh, accessible taste to the contemporary sounds of jazz. Longtime friends saxophonist Charlie Skaret, bassist Kai Knudson, and guitarist Isaac Gelfman have shared a passion for music making over the years. Their trio grew in 2024 to include drummer Jared Ammon and pianist John Kuntz, and Side.Door was created. Playing mostly original work, their lineup brings each member’s unique artistry to life. 

Drawing inspiration from Duke Ellington to Bill Withers, Franz Liszt to Frank Sinatra, and a flair of Troye Sivan, Side.Door fuses an upbeat, unique musical blend of Jazz, Classical, and Pop with their own contemporary take. Side.Door makes an open, accessible and lasting connection with their audience. 

Based in Minneapolis, MN, Side.Door performs throughout the Twin Cities, including at uptown PorchFest, Urban Forage Winery and Cider House, Driftwood Char Bar, the White Squirrel, Amsterdam Bar and Hall, Aster Cafe, and more. Whether innovating new jazz standard arrangements or debuting original compositions, this band is making waves in the contemporary jazz-fusion landscape.

Simple Motions is a St. Cloud, Minnesota–based indie rock band crafting melodic, catchy, and jangly songs that blend modern indie sensibilities with a vivid streak of eighties nostalgia. Our music has been described as cinematic, something that comes from Avdem’s background as a frustrated filmmaker. After one of our shows, someone actually told us our music sounds like a “1980s John Hughes movie,” and honestly, we’ll take that. Even with our slacker-leaning influences, we’re always writing, always recording, always finding new ways to shape what Simple Motions is becoming. At the end of the day, we’re just fans of music making music—DIY, Minnesota-born, and constantly creating.

Slash Fire was formed in the fall of 2024, this Minneapolis-based punk rock band brings together veterans from punk and heavy music scenes across the Midwest and Pacific Northwest. Fronted by powerhouse vocalist Tammy, the band blends pop punk hooks, melodic hardcore energy, and hard-driving riffs that drift into classic hard rock, metal, and stoner rock territory — all tied together by a raw, emotional delivery and a live show built to hit hard.

The lineup features dual guitar attacks from Jeremy (formerly of Seattle’s Well Adjusted and Chicago’s Audio Violence) and Eric (formerly of Iowa punk outfit Back Door Betty), backed by drummer Matt (ex-The Narrows, Seattle) and bassist Mongo, known from Minneapolis heavyweights No Funeral and Carcinolith.

Since forming, the band has quickly built momentum playing shows throughout the Twin Cities, Chicago, and Iowa, earning a reputation for loud sets, melodic grit, and a sound that refuses to stay in one lane. Their self-titled 6-song EP captures that mix of melody, aggression, and heavy rock influence while showcasing Tammy’s commanding vocal style at the center of it all.

Solana & The Sunsets – Artist Bio
Solana is a Latino American artist from South Minneapolis creating indie R&B; music centered around
heartfelt love songs and smooth, melodic grooves. His music blends soulful vocals with modern R&B;
and indie influences.
Live, Solana performs with his band The Sunsets, bringing his recordings to life with a vibrant and
engaging full-band sound. Together they deliver energetic performances that mix soulful melodies,
groove-driven rhythms, and a warm, uplifting stage presence.
Solana & The Sunsets have performed at numerous events around the Twin Cities, including Sota
Sound Music Festival and the Day of the Dead Music Festival. Solana has also performed the national
anthem at a Minnesota Lynx game, showcasing his powerful vocal presence to a large audienc

Squinny is a Minneapolis psych fuzz four-piece. Synth and riff-heavy, the group’s high-energy performances are home to both dancing and head-banging. Their combination of crushing rhythms and giant melodies is reminiscent of King Crimson a la Black Sabbath.

bandcamp_link: Stay at Home Astronaut are a three-piece post-rock band that incorporate elements of punk, prog, and
bio: Stay at Home Astronaut are a three-piece post-rock band that incorporate elements of punk, prog, and math rock to create music that is equally weird as it is catchy.

genre: Original and Ancestral South Louisiana Sounds
bio: T Marie & Bayou Juju  channel Ancestral and Next Generation South Louisiana Sounds… This band serves up a fresh take on traditional  Cajun, Creole, Lala-Zydeco, Swamp Pop, Blues, and New Orleans R n B ….  and then wows you with new original songs imbued with that good juju from the bayou. Check out their albums featuring everything from acoustic improv in an empty cathedral …  to live shows from the sweaty dancefloors of dive bars …  to the sounds of a seven piece band rocking a festival on the banks of the Mississippi River.  This band promises a haunting taste of Louisiana past and present, and delivers an eclectic mix that stirs every chakra. Grab your sshrimp boots and dancing shoes, and follow them wherever they go... from the bayous to tours in the Northeast, Midwest, California, France, and Spain.

We’re a local Twin Cities jugband that started off with a couple of friends who’ve been in many bands together over the last 25 years from punk rock to metal, found our people at the MN Jugband Competition and decided to keep it going as a full time thing now for the last four years.  Adding folks as the flavor keeps developing; we have a tight group and love the campfire sing along feel of the crowd when we play.  Some of us even make our own instruments along the way.

Tarias and the Sound is a Minnesota-based fusion blues project led by Tony Omodt-Lopez, built around live collaboration and real-time connection. Each performance features a rotating lineup of Minnesota musicians, blending blues, jazz, rock, R&B, and funk into a one-of-a-kind experience shaped by the room and the audience.

The Tribe is a Minnesota-based record label and artist collective built on collaboration, storytelling, and shared growth. Led by Tarli, the collective brings together a dynamic group of independent artists including Wes., Graydon Francis, Stefan Wolf, IAMKAYE, MidiEvil, and Diatonic. Together, they create a sound that moves fluidly across Hip-Hop, R&B, Afrobeat, Chillwave, Neo Soul, and Future Beats—blending live performance energy with intentional, emotionally grounded music.

What started as years of organic collaboration—through studio sessions, live shows, and touring—evolved into something bigger. The Tribe was formed to unify that momentum: a platform where each artist can grow individually while contributing to something collective. At its core, The Tribe is about ownership, elevation, and creating space for artists to be fully seen—both on their own and as part of a larger movement.
If you come to a Denim Boys show and don't have fun you can either sue them or come to their house, take your shirt off, and fight them. Also, they are The World's Most Successful Band™️

The Flying T is a Minneapolis based string band that plays original Americana/Antifolk music, and carefully curated covers
in an all-acoustic style. Their first album is due out in 2026. Humor is an important part of our connection to the audience. We have a track on the Minnesota Musical Resistance Compilation album.

The Grainbelters are six friends who started playing together in 1999 and found it impossible to stop. Arisen from the mean streets of Mendota Heights, the band has grown and broadened over the last 26 years to share a love of all things Americana, playing original music and some covers pulling from country, rhythm and blues, ballads, other regional American dialects, and of course, rock and roll.

Maybe it's because the band is fueled by cheap beer and quality whiskey, but when the Hamm Sammies set out to write country music, their groove strayed from the lines. They gravitated toward a more syncopated, swampy sound: country music played in between the cracks.

Their music channels the grit of Tyler Childers, the groove of Booker T. & the MG’s, the looseness of Dr. John, and the tension of the Pixies’ quiet-to-chaos transitions. Blending these influences of honkytonk twang, Memphis soul, low down blues, and even a dash of Sonny Rollins (especially his Way Out West era), their arrangements get people out of their seats. If they’re not careful, audiences tend to shed their Midwestern stoicism during a Sammies set.
The Hazy Phase is a gritty blues rock trio hailing from the Minneapolis area, known for fusing blues raw slide guitar work with heavy rhythms and vintage soul.

The Japhies pick up where classic rock radio has left us, wondering what has happened to the authenticity of rock bands. Difﬁcult to describe but undeniable when witnessed live, The Japhies have revived the corpse of rock and roll, bringing a visceral, raw energy to live performances as well as dynamic songwriting, reminding fans that it's okay to turn it up to 11. Their music, performances, and persona have inspired a wide array of classiﬁcations.

Reunited after 13 years, The Japhies have digitally reissued their debut EP from 2011  and are set to release their full length record “Allegations” in 2026. Produced by Ed Ackerson at Flowers Studio back in 2012. With the help of new bass player Lee Carter
(4onthefloor), The Japhies are hitting the stage again with their raucous live shows. Long Live Rock N Roll!

Formed in Minneapolis in 2024, The Midnight Current is a three-piece rock band built on tension between
chaos and control, noise and intention. Blending psychedelic rock with blues grit and folk sensibility, their
sound is equal parts instinct and precision - it’s loud, deliberate, and hard to pin down. Their songs swing between playful and cutting, taking on love, nature, self-confidence, and the absurdity of
modern social conventions without settling into one lane for long. There’s humor in it, but also a refusal to
look away.
Frontman Andy Caron leads with sharp songwriting and a vocal delivery that shifts from intimate to
unhinged. Bassist Cody Bryan pushes melodic lines to the front, blurring rhythm and lead, while drummer
Andrew Teunis holds it all together in the pocket as the band stretches and reshapes songs in real time.
Known for improvisation and raw interplay, The Midnight Current treats structure as a starting point, not a
boundary. Their debut album Swell Sounds captures that push and pull, but the band is at its core: loud,
unpredictable, and fully alive on stage.

The Mood Swings are a female fronted, garage driven rock band from Minneapolis, serving up catchy songs, loud guitars, and a high energy set. Featuring members of BNLX, 27 Various, and Melismatics, they're longtime Twin Cities musicians proud to be part of the Susstones Records community.

The Quantum Mechanics are an inter-dimensional jam band performing original fusion music based on assumptions, guesswork and pseudo-science, with songs about subatomic particles, parallel dimensions, alternative realities and inter-dimensional travel. Join The Quantum Mechanics for a wild psychedelic, quasi-scientific, inter-dimensional romp through the nether regions of the space-time continuum.

Providing a soundtrack to the dystopian future we deserve.
The Real Chuck NORAD is a Minneapolis-based crew of musicians, blending experimental funk, trip-hop, and brass-fueled psychedelia. —equal parts interstellar mayhem and Minneapolis soul.

The Sound Insurgent (TSI) is a DJ from Sioux City, Iowa with over 20 years of experience on the decks, known for vinyl-driven sets blending techno, drum & bass, house, hip-hop, and classic 70s & 80s 45s.

Fueled by a lifelong passion for music, TSI has built a reputation as a trusted local favorite with an eclectic and diverse sound, an expert ability to read the crowd, and a style that makes every performance unique and energetic.

Starting on vinyl turntables and evolving with modern DJ technology, The Sound Insurgent continues to push the craft forward while respecting the roots of DJ culture.

TSI has performed throughout the Midwest and shared stages with artists such as Lazer Rocket Arm, D.A.D., TreyLane and Ally Brooke.

The Stinging Nettles is an all-female, 5-piece rock/indie/punk group performing original music (and some covers) in the Twin Cities. The Nettles formed in June of 2024, and in that time has impressed audiences with their high-energy, captivating performance style and catchy music at numerous venues. You can find them on Instagram at "stingingnettlesmpls." The Nettles is proud to boast an all-female lineup creating original music. The Nettles recorded an EP in January that will be released soon!

The Stress of Her Regard, Ciaran Daly (vocals, guitar), Kristopher Johnson (guitar), Criostoir Daly (bass) and Eric Wilson (drums, vocals) is a rock band based in Minneapolis, MN. The band maintains a reputation for energetic live shows, and performs regularly at top Twin Cities venues (7th Street Entry, Turf Club). They were featured as a 2015 Minneapolis Are You Local? finalist for Best New Band and have played supporting slots for touring acts including Moving Units, Marmozets, The Suburbs, and The Twilight Sad. They have been featured in regional festivals including Go Show 1 with K. Flay, New Politics and BANKS, the Midwest Music Showcase, Basilica Block Party, and others.

In 2015, the band released their debut EP, Sport Marriage, which featured production from BJ Burton (Poliça), Dave Trumfio (Jesus & Mary Chain), Tony Lash (The Dandy Warhols, Elliott Smith), and Ed Ackerson (Joseph Arthur), and saw singles ‘Sport Marriage’ and ‘The Ballad of Josie and Davey (Legalize Gay)’ become favorites and garner radio play and streaming around the world.

The band’s self-titled debut full-length was released in 2021. Produced, mixed and mastered by Ed Ackerson at Flowers Studio in Minneapolis, the record grew out of COVID-19 to find its footing with audiences around the globe.

New single, ‘Robot Dogs,’ released July 24, 2026, expands upon the band’s Jesus and Mary Chain-meets-Jim Jarmush aesthetic with two songs and a remix written against the backdrop of brutal ICE incursions, the rise of the billionaire class, and literal fire-breathing robotic dogs legally produced and sold to the public in the United States. The accompanying B-Side, “Ice Water Mansions,” takes the listener on a haunting trip to the shores of Lake Superior, where the violence of winter is balanced by its frigid beauty, and where the frozen lake expanse allows one’s past to rear up to haunt them.

Threads Electric is an indie rock/electro pop 4-piece from Minneapolis, Minnesota.​
Multi-instrumentalists Joe Capacete and Brian Perry recorded their debut album in Brian's basement. They worked with producer Yoo Soo Kim and created a collection of indie rock/ pop anthems. They brought on new friends Alex Cheng (bass) and Katie Rider (synth) in the summer of 2025 and it’s been all vibes ever since. 
Everything is interim. The breath in our lungs sustains us, but we let it go as soon as we take it in. Our bones form the framework of our bodies, but eventually fade to dust. In between, we have moments we carry with us: all-nighters, road trips, a first kiss, a sunset stroll. These songs explore the tenuous connection between the temporary and the transcendent. This is our breath. These are our bones.

Based in the Twin Cities, Tinynormous crafts an atmospheric instrumental journey that balances technical sophistication with raw emotional depth. Their sound is defined by a "harmony, guitars, and sensitivity" that feels both warm and inviting, seamlessly blending jazz fusion complexity with melodic immediacy.

Following the release of their debut full-length 12" vinyl last year, the band continues their momentum with the January release of their new live CD, All Are Welcome. Whether through sprawling instrumentals or carefully layered beats, Tinynormous delivers a wide-reaching sonic experience that keeps listeners engaged from start to finish.

Topiary Blush is a four-piece alternative soul rock group with influences ranging from Hiatus Kaiyote, The Police, Brittany Howard, and Jazz/R&B classics; elements of heaviness emerge when the songs call for them, echoing the passion and excitement that is present within the band.

Shaped during their time at the U, Van Cleaver is a 3-piece built on years of playing together. Their sound moves between driving alt-rock and quieter, folk-tinged tunes, drawing from the likes of Green Day, Muse, Rage Against the Machine, and Taylor Swift. Mixed-race an unapologetically left, they've played weddings, birthdays, protests, and anywhere else that will have them.

We are an all original Native American rock band from different tribal heritage backgrounds based out of Minneapolis Minnesota and we are bringing our own brand of epic, spiritual, and deeply moving rock to the masses.

genre: cute gaze mew-mew metal ethereal indie
bio:
Ditch Pigeon is the heart-wrenching songwriting of lead guitarist Hayley Anne punched up with the punk styling of her fiance, Morgan Liluna, behind the kit and rounded out with the musicianship and undeniable stage presence of scene couple Nathan Honeypants on bass and Anna Herr on violin. “mew mew metal” evokes both the intricacies of the strings and harmonies as well as the heavier nature of the guitar tone and drum parts while nodding to the wholesome, sometimes cutesy, familial nature of the musicians as a group of friends.

Like the greatest jam bands, Hayley arranges and rearranges both the setlist and the lineup on a regular basis. Having a shared musical language with a variety of collaborators outside of the core quintet that is Ditch Pigeon, every live show is unique. Tempos are slowed for emotional value in a solo set, crescendos grow greater in full band shows, and the obvious chemistry between her and her many collaborators is infectious. To be compelling night after night in so many different lineups is a challenge she easily overcomes, and it makes her live performances as special as her songs.

Emmy Woods (she/they) was born and raised on an old dirt road in rural North Dakota and currently resides in Saint Paul, MN. With hints of country, folk, and blues, Emmy’s songs showcase her knack for storytelling, her strengths in musical artistry, and her ethereal voice. Drawing on a range of influences including Billie Holiday, Emmylou Harris, & Against Me, Emmy has shared stages with such talents as Melissa Carper, Sarah Morris, Ryan  Young of Trampled by Turtles, and Cam Whitcomb, to name a few. Emmy began writing at 13, however, her music remained unreleased and rarely performed until 2023, when she burst out of her living room and onto the Minnesota music scene with the release of 3 recorded collections. Undeniably prolific, she has since released several singles and an EP. Performing anywhere that’ll have her, from dive bars and markets to ballrooms and festivals, Woods continues to gain momentum with her witty & captivating repertoire, her disarmingly down to earth charm, and her genre-bending sound.

pity party is a Minneapolis based indie alt rock band. They use music as a way to express their outrage for what is going on in US and global politics. 
Their music brings together a wide range of musical backgrounds and influences from the early 2000s to craft songs with pop sheen and rock and roll heart. Come party with pity party.
